paper_title: Schuldenbremse und öffentliche Investitionen: Erwiderung auf Mühlenweg et al. (2024)
caption: Fiskalregel-Index des IWF
model_annotation: Both diagrams share the same x-axis, labeled with years from 1995 to 2020 at intervals of 5 years, and have a similar structure. The left y-axis in both diagrams represents the 'IWF Fiskalindex' (IMF Fiscal Index), ranging from 0 to 2.5 on the left diagram and from -5 to 1.5 on the right diagram, with tick labels at intervals of 0.5. The right y-axis represents 'Schuldenquote Gesamtstaat' (Total Government Debt Ratio) on the left diagram, ranging from 60 to 120, and 'Schuldenquote Zentralstaat' (Central Government Debt Ratio) on the right diagram, ranging from 30 to 70, both with tick labels at intervals of 20 and 10 respectively. The left diagram displays two lines: a blue line with triangle markers representing the 'IWF Fiskalindex,' which starts at around 0 in 1995, peaks at approximately 1 in 2008, and then decreases to around 0.1 in 2020, and a purple line representing 'Schuldenquote Gesamtstaat,' which starts at around 60 in 1995, increases to around 85 in 2015, and then rises sharply to around 110 in 2020. Red and blue triangle markers are also plotted, representing 'Schuldenquote Gesamtstaat' and 'IWF Fiskalindex' respectively, with varying values over the years. The right diagram similarly displays two lines: a blue line representing the 'IWF Fiskalindex,' which starts at around -4 in 1995, peaks at approximately 0.5 in 2009, and then decreases to around -3.5 in 2020, and a purple line representing 'Schuldenquote Zentralstaat,' which starts at around 40 in 1995, remains relatively stable until 2008, and then rises to around 65 in 2020, with red and blue triangle markers representing 'Schuldenquote Zentralstaat' and 'IWF Fiskalindex' respectively.
